content.text: The document expressly disclaims minimum commitments. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 meets the preferred position outright: there is no minimum quantity or purchase commitment, Customer pays only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form, and declining to place further Orders is expressly not a breach or shortfall. Section 7.1 reinforces this by barring any unstated minimum-use or similar charge, and Section 12 records that Customer has made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment. No take-or-pay, committed-spend, or volume cap on Customer usage appears anywhere; Order Forms (Section 4.1) require mutual signature for any quantity change, and Section 8.2 lets Customer exit on thirty days' non-renewal notice. The Section 22 "shortfall" reference is an audit true-up for over-usage, not a minimum commitment, and the Section 7.7 late-payment charge is a payment-default term outside this rule. No redline required.
